title: Alexander Wolitzky, MIT 14.121: Lectures 3–4, Consumer Theory (Fall 2015)
use: Primary course-method reference for indirect utility, budget multipliers and Roy's identity, expenditure/Hicksian demand, price concavity, Shephard's lemma, dual identities and Slutsky restrictions. Chapter independently supplies its own finite-dimensional proofs, explicit target and positive-derivative restrictions, and numerical cases.
verification: Retrieved the actual official 42-page PDF and inspected the substantive text of printed pages 13–41, with prior budget/existence context on pages 7–11. Checked formula and hypothesis scope for derivative identities and correspondence duality. Did not claim exhaustive verification of every statement in the source or adopt abbreviated hypotheses without the chapter's attainable-target and v_m > 0 qualifications. The two chapter worked cases, quasilinear boundary example and all exercises are original. No source exam/problem set copied.

title: Alexander Wolitzky, MIT 14.121: Lecture 5, Applications of Consumer Theory (Fall 2015)
use: Primary method reference for expenditure-based money metrics, reference-price choices, CV/EV and compensated versus Marshallian areas. The chapter explicitly defines losses as positive, reversing the source's signed-gain definitions; no historical price-index estimates are imported.
verification: Retrieved the actual official 30-page PDF and inspected printed pages 3–11 covering ordinal-invariance reasoning, welfare definitions and areas. The source uses EV=e(p0,u1)-m and CV=m-e(p1,u0); our opposite convention is stated beside both indifference equations and the citation. PDF text extraction disrupts some displayed integral notation, so all signs, integral endpoints and example values were independently derived from expenditure definitions rather than inferred from garbled layout. No whole-document or visual-publication QA claim.
